name: VALEPASKA
description: Valepaska is a Finnish bluffing/shedding game variant of Paskahousu. 3-8 players. Cards played face-down with declarations — players can LIE about what they played. Other players call 'Valepaska!' to challenge. Wrong challenger picks up pile; caught liar picks up pile. Special cards: 2s (supercards), 10s clear pile, Aces clear face cards, four-of-a-kind clears.

content.text: Valepaska is a Finnish bluffing/shedding game variant of Paskahousu. 3-8 players. Cards played face-down with declarations — players can LIE about what they played. Other players call 'Valepaska!' to challenge. Wrong challenger picks up pile; caught liar picks up pile. Special cards: 2s (supercards), 10s clear pile, Aces clear face cards, four-of-a-kind clears.

Valepaska is a Finnish game of bluff, a variation of Paskahousu. The word valepaska means "lying shit"; the game is also known as Kusetuspaskahousu. It was previously listed under the name Paskahousu on some rule sites. All cards are played face down and players announce what they are playing; they may tell the truth or lie, but if challenged and caught lying they must pick up the pile. The rules are based on contributions from Ola Rinta-Koski and Mikko Jutila.
Three or more players; best with four or five.
A standard deck of 52 cards is used. Cards rank from high to low: 2, A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3.
Dealer gives each player five cards; the remaining cards form a face-down stock pile.

items.text: Four twos do not clear: Some play that four twos do not clear the pile; the next player could pick it up or play another card claiming it was also a two.
Only black 2s, 10s and Aces special: Only black 2s, 10s and Aces have a special role. Red tens and aces are ordinary and do not clear the pile; red twos are the lowest cards, below threes.
Jokers or spare cards: Some include jokers or other spare cards in the deck; they have no rank and can only be got rid of by lying about what they are.
